page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.large is an entry-level virtual server powered by a shared Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, alongside 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core). It features 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and supports AVX, AVX512F, and AES instruction sets. KVM hypervisor virtualizes the underlying hardware, which has 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, no local storage, and zero included public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.n4.large demonstrates lower-tier computational and memory throughput due to its shared CPU allocation model. Single-core performance registered a stress-ng score of 1107.98 and a Geekbench score of 957.0, while multi-core stress-ng reached 2199.5. Memory tests yielded 17.08 GB/sec uncached read and 14.55 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth. PassMark CPU and memory scores were 2677.34 and 974.98 respectively. Redis SET operations reached 3.0 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 1.82 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU resources, lack of bundled local storage, and minimal network baseline, the instance delivers a low resource footprint focused on qualitative cost efficiency. It is best suited for basic general-purpose tasks, lightweight web serving, low-concurrency background utilities, and small dev/test environments where dedicated processor allocation is not required.
